Index RSI Report

Updated September 22, 2026 · S&P 500, Nasdaq 100, S&P/TSX Composite, Russell 2000

These charts show how stretched each major index is compared with its own recent history, using the Relative Strength Index (RSI). RSI runs from 0 to 100 and compares the size of recent gains with recent losses. High readings mean the index has run up hard and may be overbought. Low readings mean it has sold off sharply and may be oversold.

Each index has two views. The weekly RSI uses the last 14 weeks and picks up shorter swings. The 1-year RSI uses the last 52 weeks and tracks the longer trend. It moves more slowly, so its oversold and overbought levels sit closer together. Each index has its own levels, marked by the dashed lines, because some indices run hotter or calmer than others. For example, the weekly S&P 500 is oversold below 40 and overbought above 75.

Oversold week   Overbought week   Charts show each index's full available history. The current week uses the latest close until the week ends.
